title: Lesson 1 Quiz: Externalities and Market Failure
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin); do not give to students.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best example of a negative externality?

choices.text: A bakery raises its bread prices, so customers pay more
A neighbor's all-night party keeps the student next door awake
Buying expensive sneakers shrinks your own allowance
A company pays its employees their monthly salaries

questions.prompt: A beekeeper's bees pollinate a nearby orchard, and the orchard's fruit harvest grows. The orchard owner pays the beekeeper nothing. Which statement best describes this situation?

choices.text: It is a negative externality, so honey tends to be produced above the socially optimal amount
It is not an externality, because the orchard owner did not pay anything for it
It is a positive externality, so beekeeping tends to fall below the socially optimal amount
The bees are a common resource, so they tend to be overused by nearby farms

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A coal-fired power plant spends $80 on fuel, labor, and other costs to generate 1 MWh of electricity, and its air pollution causes $30 of harm per MWh to nearby residents. What is the social cost of 1 MWh of electricity, in dollars? (Enter a number only.)
Producing a certain good creates a negative externality. Without government intervention, which statement best describes the market outcome?

choices.text: The market quantity is smaller than the socially optimal quantity
The market quantity equals the socially optimal quantity; just the prices differ
The social-cost curve lies below the supply curve
The market quantity is larger than the socially optimal quantity

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: In a market with demand Qd = 80 − P and supply Qs = P, every unit produced creates an external cost of $10. By how many units does the market quantity exceed the socially optimal quantity? (Enter a number only.)
